Angles written ∠ are read from the figure. ∡(a, b) is the angle through which line a must be turned counter-clockwise to become parallel to b, taken modulo 180°; ∡XYZ means ∡(YX, YZ). These angles do not depend on how the figure is drawn. Directed angles are needed only in steps 5, 7 and 8, where the figure-angle form would depend on the configuration. Let Ω be the circumcircle of triangle ABC, with center O; N, S, E, P lie on Ω. Let ω₁ be the circle (BDL), with center O₁; P lies on ω₁.

Plan: it suffices to show that XA = XP and ∡IAP = ∡APX.

1. We show that NB = NC:

∠NBC = ∠NAC    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∠BAN    [AI bisects ∠BAC]
     = ∠BCN    [N, C, B, A on Ω]

Hence NB = NC. (1)

2. By (1), OB = OC and NB = NC, so ON is the perpendicular bisector of BC; hence ON ⟂ BC. (2)

3. We show that T, E, S, O are concyclic:

∠BTO = 90° − ∠SBE    [OT ⟂ BE]
     = 90° − ∠SNE    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∠OSE    [NS is a diameter of Ω]
     = ∠SEO    [central angle in Ω]

So T, E, S, O are concyclic. (3)

4. We show that T, P, X, O are concyclic:

∠OTX = ∠EBS + 90°    [OT ⟂ BE]
     = ∠EBP + ∠PNO + 90°    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∠EBC − ∠NPB + 180°    [ON ⟂ BC, by (2)]
     = ∠BLD − ∠NPB + 180°    [DL ∥ BC]
     = ∠NPD    [inscribed angles in ω₁]
     = ∠PBX + ∠NPX    [PX is tangent to ω₁ (tangent–chord angle)]
     = ∠PNO + ∠NPX    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∠OPX    [ON = OP]

So T, P, X, O are concyclic. (4)

5. We show that T, P, E, D are concyclic:

∡ETD = ∡EON    [T, E, S, O concyclic, by (3)]
     = ∡(OE, BC) + 90°    [ON ⟂ BC, by (2)]
     = ∡(OE, DL) + 90°    [DL ∥ BC]
     = ∡OEB + ∡BPD + 90°    [inscribed angles in ω₁]
     = ∡OEA + ∡APD + 90°    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∡EPD    [OA = OE; central angle in Ω]

So T, P, E, D are concyclic. (5)

6. We show that XA = XP:

∠AOX = ∠AOP − ∠PTB    [T, P, X, O concyclic, by (4)]
     = ∠OAE − ∠EPO    [T, P, E, D concyclic, by (5)]
     = ∠AEP    [central angle in Ω]
     = ∠BTP    [T, P, E, D concyclic, by (5)]
     = ∠XOP    [T, P, X, O concyclic, by (4)]

Radii of Ω, so △OAX ≅ △OPX. Hence XA = XP. (6)

7. We show that ∡IAP = ∡APX:

∡IAP = ∡NBP    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∡DBP + 90°    [NS is a diameter of Ω]
     = ∡DLP + 90°    [P, L, D, B on ω₁]
     = ∡(BC, LP) + 90°    [DL ∥ BC]
     = ∡(AD, LP)    [AD ⟂ BC]
     = ∡AEB + ∡BPX    [PX is tangent to ω₁ (tangent–chord angle)]
     = ∡APX    [inscribed angles in Ω] (7)

8. We show that AX bisects ∠BAC:

∡BAX = 2∡IAC + ∡CAX    [AI bisects ∠BAC]
     = ∡XAC + 2∡IAP + 2∡XPA    [XA = XP: triangle XAP is isosceles, by (6)]
     = ∡XAC    [by (7)]

Hence AX bisects ∠BAC, as required. ∎
